title: State: What It Is and How Terraform Uses It

header.html: 2d Explain how Terraform uses and manages state
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

toc.title: How Terraform uses state in the workflow
What happens if the state is lost or wrong

html:
1What state is

State is Terraform's record of the infrastructure it manages. It is a JSON file (by default terraform.tfstate in the working directory) that maps each resource in the configuration to a real object in the platform.

Purpose Meaning
Mapping Links aws_instance.web to a real instance ID
Metadata Remembers dependencies and provider information
Performance Caches attribute values so large setups do not need to query everything
Plan Terraform compares configuration, state and reality to compute what to change
Exam tip

. State maps configuration to real infrastructure. Without it Terraform cannot tell what it already created.

2How Terraform uses state in the workflow

Command Use of state
terraform plan Reads state, refreshes it from the platform and compares with the configuration
terraform apply Changes the infrastructure and updates the state
terraform destroy Removes the resources and empties the state
terraform show Displays the state or a saved plan

3Handling state safely

Rule Why
Never edit the state file by hand A mistake can orphan or duplicate resources; use terraform state commands
State may contain secrets Passwords and keys appear in plain text; restrict access and encrypt the storage
Do not commit state to Git It can leak secrets and conflicts between people
Use a remote backend for teams Shared, locked and encrypted state (Module 13)
Back it up Remote backends can keep versions
Fact Detail
Sensitive marking sensitive = true hides values in CLI output but they remain in state
State and terraform.tfstate.backup The local backend keeps a backup of the previous state
Exam tip

. State can contain sensitive data in plain text. Marking a value sensitive does not remove it from the state file.

4What happens if the state is lost or wrong

Situation Result
State lost Terraform thinks nothing exists and tries to create everything again; you must import the resources
Resource deleted outside Terraform The next plan notices and proposes to recreate it (drift, Module 14)
Two people apply at once Conflicting updates; state locking prevents this (Module 13)
Exam tip

. Lost state means Terraform thinks nothing exists. The fix is to restore the state or import the resources, not to run apply again.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1What is the main role of the Terraform state?

  • ATo map configuration to real infrastructure
  • BTo store the provider plugins
  • CTo format the configuration files
  • DTo hold the version control history
Show the answer

Answer: A. State maps each resource in the configuration to a real object and caches its attributes.

S2A teammate wants to fix a mistake by editing terraform.tfstate with a text editor. What is the best advice?

  • AEdit the file carefully with a text editor
  • BDelete the file and run apply again
  • CUse terraform state commands instead
  • DCopy the file to every teammate
Show the answer

Answer: C. State should never be edited by hand; the terraform state commands change it safely.

S3A database password is stored in a resource attribute marked sensitive. Where can the value still be found?

  • AIn the CLI output of every plan
  • BNowhere, because it is hidden everywhere
  • CIn the provider lock file
  • DIn the state file, in plain text
Show the answer

Answer: D. Sensitive values are hidden in CLI output but remain in the state file.

S4What happens when the state file is lost and the configuration is unchanged?

  • ATerraform rebuilds the state automatically from the cloud
  • BTerraform destroys all resources immediately
  • CTerraform copies the state from the provider
  • DTerraform tries to create everything again
Show the answer

Answer: D. Without state Terraform does not know the resources exist, so it plans to create them again unless they are imported.

S5Why do teams use a remote backend for state?

  • AIt removes the need for providers
  • BIt makes plans run without any provider credentials
  • CIt allows sharing, locking and secure storage
  • DIt converts HCL to JSON
Show the answer

Answer: C. Remote backends give shared, locked and protected state for teams.

S6Which command displays the contents of the current state in a readable form?

  • Aterraform fmt
  • Bterraform init
  • Cterraform show
  • Dterraform validate
Show the answer

Answer: C. terraform show displays the state or a saved plan.

5.2 Recall questions

R1In what format is the default state file?

Show the answer

JSON, in terraform.tfstate.

R2What does state map?

Show the answer

Configuration resources to real infrastructure objects.

R3Can state contain secrets?

Show the answer

Yes, in plain text.

R4Should state be edited by hand?

Show the answer

No, use terraform state commands.

R5What does a lost state cause?

Show the answer

Terraform plans to create everything again.

R6Which command displays state?

Show the answer

terraform show.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
State JSON record mapping configuration to real objects; caches attributes
Safety never edit by hand; may hold secrets; not in Git; remote backend for teams
Lost state Terraform plans to recreate everything; import instead
Commands plan reads and refreshes; apply updates; show displays
